### [`v12.19.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.19.0): pnpm 12.19

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.18.0...v12.19.0)

pnpm 12.19.0 adds `pnpm fund`, lets the `loaded` node linker handle packages that need a build, and adds the `projectScopedOptionalPeers` setting and an experimental JSON lockfile format. It also includes a security fix: an offline install error no longer prints registry credentials. pnpm now checks the `engines` and platform fields of every workspace project, and many hoisted-linker and frozen-lockfile bugs are fixed.

##### Minor Changes

- Added `pnpm fund`, which lists the funding URLs declared by the installed dependencies in the same tree `npm fund` prints. Use `--json` for the `npm fund --json` report and `--recursive` or `--filter` to report on workspace projects. `pnpm fund <pkg>` opens the funding URL of an installed package, and `--which` picks one when it lists several [#​7354](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/7354).

- With `nodeLinker.type: loaded`, packages that need a build no longer have to be listed in `nodeLinker.excluded`. A package with a matching side-effects cache entry loads from the store. If side-effects cache reads and writes are enabled, pnpm builds an approved package once, saves the result to the side-effects cache, and then loads it from the store. This includes a build that changes no files in its package, so its script does not run again in other projects that use the same store. List a package in `sideEffectsCache.exclude` if its build must run in every project, such as a git hook installer. pnpm materializes other cache misses, packages with native `.node` addons, and their dependencies automatically.

  pnpm also scans JavaScript sources for filesystem imports and for `__dirname` or `import.meta`, and materializes matching packages. The scan does not detect computed imports. List such packages in `nodeLinker.excluded`.

- Added the `projectScopedOptionalPeers` setting. When it is `true`, a project gets a missing optional peer dependency only if the project's own dependencies install a version of it. Another workspace project's dependencies, such as its `devDependencies`, no longer supply one. `dedupePeerDependents` keeps deduplicating everything else [#​16666](https://redirect.github.com/orgs/pnpm/discussions/16666).

- Added the experimental `lockfile.format: v13` setting. With it, pnpm writes `pnpm-lock.yaml` in a JSON-like syntax, indented with tabs, with a trailing comma after every entry. The file is still valid YAML. The file has one `packages` entry per package version in place of the `packages` and `snapshots` sections, and each entry records the versions of its peer dependencies as its properties. Updating a peer dependency then changes only the lines that record its version. pnpm reads lockfiles in both formats whatever the setting is.

- `pnpm store add` now accepts directories of tarballs, such as `pnpm store add ./tarballs`, and adds every `.tgz`, `.tar.gz`, and `.tar` file inside them recursively. `pnpm store add` is now faster when it adds many packages or local tarballs [#​17875](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17875).

- With `supportedArchitectures` set, `pnpm install` and `pnpm fetch` also store, without linking them, the dependencies of the archives kept for the other listed platforms. A platform added to the setting gets its archives and their dependencies on the next install. Optional dependencies a listed platform cannot run are not stored, and one that fails to download is skipped. Dependencies from git repositories are not stored for other platforms.

- When `supportedArchitectures` names exactly one platform and not `current`, pnpm links that platform's variant of a package published with platform variants, together with that variant's dependencies. This holds for the list form and for the `os`, `cpu`, and `libc` form. A variant whose floor or ABI the listed platform does not state is not linked for it: pnpm links another variant that fits, or the version's own archive. Changing the setting, or the platform of the host, such as a `node_modules` mounted into a musl container or a Node.js with another ABI, relinks the package on the next install, even from a frozen lockfile.

- pnpm now provides a prebuilt binary for NetBSD 10 on x64 [#​17803](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17803).

##### Patch Changes

##### Security

- The error for a tarball that is missing from the store in offline mode no longer prints the credentials or token in the tarball URL.

##### Installs that failed or hung

- `pnpm install`, `pnpm ci`, and `pnpm install-test` outside a workspace now fail with `ERR_PNPM_NO_PKG_MANIFEST` when the directory has no `package.json`, `package.json5`, or `package.yaml`. They no longer create a `package.json`, a lockfile, and `node_modules` there [#​17727](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17727).

- Fixed `pnpm install` hanging when a concurrent tarball download or manifest read is cancelled while other tasks are waiting on the same archive.

- Running a global command such as `node` in a project that pins its version no longer hangs while pnpm installs that version. The hang kept starting new processes until the machine ran out of memory.

- A global command such as `node` now runs the version a project pins when `PNPM_CONFIG_LOCKFILE_DIR`, `PNPM_CONFIG_VIRTUAL_STORE_ONLY`, or `PNPM_CONFIG_SYMLINK` is set in the environment. Before, the dispatch failed with "the installed node executable is not under" the store.

- `pnpm install` now fetches fresh metadata for a package when a version allowed by `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` is missing from the cached metadata. Before, it could fail with `ERR_PNPM_NO_MATCHING_VERSION` without contacting the registry [#​17723](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17723).

- A `${VAR}` placeholder in a registry URL in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or the project `.npmrc` now fails the command. pnpm does not expand environment variables in these files. Before, pnpm ignored such a URL and resolved packages from another registry, such as npmjs.org. pnpm now warns when it ignores a placeholder in a proxy, `pnprServer`, or `userAgent` setting in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` [#​17762](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17762).

- Fixed local package installs failing while a workspace lockfile is being written.

- `pnpm self-update` and switching to the `packageManager` version now work behind a proxy that ends a response by closing the TLS connection without a `close_notify` alert. The registry signature check failed there with `ERR_PNPM_PNPM_ENGINE_IDENTITY_UNVERIFIABLE` [#​17763](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17763).

- A package tarball that keeps failing to download now fails the install after `fetchRetries` retries. pnpm used to download it again with a second full set of retries, which doubled the wait. The error now names the actual download failure.

- When the native binary of the pnpm version a project pins fails to download, pnpm now reports the download error. It used to report only that no native binary was found for the host.

- POSIX bin shims and the `pnpm`, `pn`, `pnpx`, and `pnx` launchers now run inside a Nix build on macOS with the sandbox enabled. Installing again replaces the shims already in `node_modules` [#​17750](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17750).

- Fixed pnpm leaving process pipes open after it exits on macOS [pnpm/tasks#229](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/229).

##### Engines and platform checks

- `pnpm install`, `pnpm add`, `pnpm update`, and `pnpm remove` now check the `engines`, `os`, `cpu`, and `libc` fields of every workspace project, including the workspace root. `pnpm run -r` and `pnpm exec -r` check them before running anything. An incompatible `engines.pnpm` fails the command. An incompatible `engines.node` prints a warning, or fails the command with `engineStrict` enabled. An unsupported platform prints a warning. Issues.Title: bug(snack-bar,bottom-sheet): Idiomatic configuration not compatible with new ESLint strict type-checked rule
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

`typescript-eslint` [version 8.0.73](https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/releases/tag/v8.73.0) was released on Nov 16, 2026 with a new [`no-unsafe-class-instance-assignment` rule](https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/pull/12907) that flags situations where "object literal is used where an instance of class (...) is expected".

Idiomatic configuration of Snackbars or Bottom Sheets (and maybe other components) is achieved (and documented) with the use of a last parameter that falls into that case, because `MatSnackBarConfig`,  `MatBottomSheetConfig`, etc. are defined as `class` instead of `interface`.

As a consequence, a simple project with Material Angular + Typescript-ESLint project with strict type-checked linting enabled reports an error where using the components with the configuration parameter:

```typescript
snackBar.open(
  'Message archived',
  'Undo',
  { duration: 3000 } // Lint error: This object literal is used where an instance of class `MatSnackBarConfig<any>` is expected.
);
```


### Reproduction

StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/edit/9uwq3dhq?file=eslint.config.mjs,src%2Fmain.ts
Steps to reproduce:
1. Run `npm run lint`


### Expected Behavior

There is (presumably?) no reason to define the parameters (`MatSnackBarConfig`,  `MatBottomSheetConfig`...) as classes, interfaces should be used instead.

### Actual Behavior

Parameters are defined as classes, so the strict linting rule disallows the use of object literals.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2
- CDK/Material: 22.3
- Browser(s): N/A
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): N/A

Issues.Title: fix(material/dialog): prevent visual jump by removing open class together with closing class
Issues.Body:
When `_startExitAnimation()` is called, `mdc-dialog--open` was previously removed synchronously while `mdc-dialog--closing` was scheduled in a `requestAnimationFrame` callback.

When `close()` is called from within a `requestAnimationFrame` callback (such as during zoneless change detection scheduling or reactive effect updates), the nested rAF is deferred to the next frame. During that intermediate frame, the dialog container renders with neither class, applying the base un-opened styles (`scale(0.8)` / `opacity: 0`) and causing the dialog surface to visibly shrink and then snap back when `mdc-dialog--closing` is applied.

### Solution

Remove `mdc-dialog--open` and add `mdc-dialog--closing` together within the `requestAnimationFrame` callback so the container transitions directly from the open state to the closing state without an intermediate class-less frame. When animations are disabled, `mdc-dialog--open` is removed immediately in the non-animated branch.

### Verification

- Ran Prettier format check: passed (clean formatting).
- TypeScript compile / typecheck (`tsc -p src/material/tsconfig.json --noEmit`): clean on dialog files (0 errors).
- Added unit test in `src/material/dialog/dialog.spec.ts` asserting that `mdc-dialog--open` is not removed prematurely before the closing animation frame executes.

Fixes #34123

Issues.Title: fix(cdk/text-field): defer autosize checks until view initialization
Issues.Body:
## Summary

`CdkTextareaAutosize` can cache the textarea line height during its first `ngDoCheck`, before dynamic host classes have been applied. With `matInput` inside `mat-form-field`, this means measuring the browser default font instead of the inherited font. The resulting minimum and maximum heights remain incorrect until a window resize clears the cache.

Skip automatic checks until the view has initialized, allowing the existing `ngAfterViewInit` resize to perform the initial measurement after host bindings have been applied.

For example, a textarea with a 50px line height and limits of 2–5 rows now starts with `min-height: 100px` and `max-height: 250px`.

Fixes #33944.

## Testing

Added regression tests for both a CDK textarea with a dynamic host class and a `matInput` textarea inside `mat-form-field`.

- Without the fix: both new tests fail; the existing 130 tests pass.
- With the fix: all 132 tests pass in Chromium (28 CDK text-field and 104 Material input tests).
- Existing coverage includes initial content and placeholder sizing, row limits, programmatic value changes, window resizing, and disabling/re-enabling autosize.
- Repository formatting applied to all changed files.

```sh
pnpm bazel test //src/cdk/text-field:unit_tests_chromium //src/material/input:unit_tests_chromium --test_output=errors
```

Issues.Title: bug(material/core): dark on-surface-variant uses neutral-variant 90 instead of 80
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

18.1.x

### Description

In the dark scheme, `on-surface-variant` maps to `neutral-variant` tone 90 ([`_md-sys-color.scss` L24](https://github.com/angular/components/blob/fcec64761/src/material/core/tokens/m3/_md-sys-color.scss#L24)). The Material color spec maps it to tone 80:

- [material-color-utilities `color_spec_2021.ts`](https://github.com/material-foundation/material-color-utilities/blob/main/typescript/dynamiccolor/color_spec_2021.ts): `onSurfaceVariant` → `tone: (s) => s.isDark ? 80 : 30`, unchanged since 2023.
- [material-web tokens v0_192](https://github.com/material-components/material-web/blob/main/tokens/versions/v0_192/_md-sys-color.scss): `neutral-variant80`.
- The `theme-color` schematic in this repo bundles material-color-utilities and therefore generates tone 80, so its output disagrees with the system tokens in the same package.

Tone 90 came in with #29655, which followed #29577. That issue relied on Theme Builder screenshots, and the Theme Builder labeled the dark `On Surface Var.` swatch "NV-90". That label was wrong: the swatch itself is tone 80, as already reported in material-foundation/material-theme-builder#301 (May 2024). The pixels in the screenshot attached to #29577 confirm this. The same PR changed `surface-container-highest` because of a mislabeled swatch, and #29902 reverted that change.

Because the tones are equal, `on-surface` and `on-surface-variant` render identically in the dark scheme whenever the neutral and neutral-variant palettes are close or equal. As a result, form field placeholders look like entered values, and labels and hint texts lose their visual hierarchy.

### Reproduction

No StackBlitz reproduction: the wrong value is a static token mapping and can be read directly in [`_md-sys-color.scss` L24](https://github.com/angular/components/blob/fcec64761/src/material/core/tokens/m3/_md-sys-color.scss#L24).

To see the effect:

1. Generate a theme with `ng generate @angular/material:theme-color` and the same color for neutral and neutral-variant, e.g. `#ececed`.
2. Render a `mat-form-field` with `appearance="outline"`, a placeholder and `floatLabel="always"`, next to a filled one, in the dark scheme.

### Expected Behavior

`--mat-sys-on-surface-variant` resolves to `neutral-variant` tone 80 in the dark scheme. Placeholders are visibly dimmer than entered values.

### Actual Behavior

`--mat-sys-on-surface-variant` resolves to tone 90, the same tone as `--mat-sys-on-surface`. Placeholders and values are indistinguishable.

### Environment

- Angular Material: 22.2.6
- Still present on `main` (fcec64761)
